rule: Player statuses are rows in a duration table: a short tag, colour, flags and optional end messages. Each increase names a cap in turns; the stored value is turns times 10 aut. Fear is a list of sources: the first source sets 7 turns, each further source adds 5 turns, the cap is 12, and fear ends only when no source remains. Stun immunity, given after some disables, blocks later paralysis, sleep and daze. Monster enchantments of the same kind merge by adding degree (capped at 4) and duration (capped at 30000 aut). Stagger removes energy after a concussive stumble. Knockback chance depends on the size difference. Bleed is a retired enum under a legacy version guard and has no live use in this tree.
keep: Source-count fear: each attacker adds a bounded amount; fear ends when the last source leaves
Short tag per status with a sign colour
Expiry suffix on the tag (expiring) and a prefix on the long text, so the warning survives without colour
Stun immunity after a disable, so a chain of disables cannot lock the player
Stagger that costs energy but does not lock the target
change: Trickster roll (one in three, random effect) is too random for a fast phone duel; pick the effect in data
Drop bleed from our plan: the donor retired it
Use our own tag text and names; do not copy the donor's tags
Numbers are ours; the donor values are GPL code and not copied
Bound the fear list to max three attackers and show the count on the chip
look_test: On the existing duel scene, spawn three enemies in view. Each adds to one Fear chip. Show a count (x1, x2, x3) and the turns left, with an expiring form in the last turns. Compare the summed chip with a single chip that ignores the count. Dom judges whether he can tell how many are scaring him and when it ends, at 375 wide, without a number.
